title: The AI-First Tech Function: What CEOs Need to Know
gist: BCG argues agentic AI forces CTOs/CIOs to move from service providers to strategic C-suite partners across three pillars (AI-first tech function, AI-first tech estate, C-suite partnership), citing 2-5x faster delivery, 30-70% productivity gains, ~40% token-cost cuts via CFO-led spend governance, and 89% of organizations hit by AI-enabled attacks.

insights.claim: BCG argues agentic AI requires the CTO/CIO role to expand into three pillars: accelerating AI-first technology inside the tech function, architecting an AI-first tech estate, and becoming a strategic AI partner in the C-suite.
insights.speaker: Joppe Bijlsma
insights.so_what: Use as a scorecard for judging whether a company's tech leadership is set up to capture AI value versus competitors.
insights.locator: Agentic AI is transforming the tech function

insights.claim: BCG says the strategic-partner pillar is the most critical: CTOs/CIOs must shift from service providers without a seat at the strategy table to C-suite partners driving AI-first transformation, and CEOs must champion that shift.
insights.speaker: Joppe Bijlsma
insights.so_what: Governance signal: firms where the tech leader sits in strategy discussions are more likely to scale agentic AI beyond pilots.
insights.quote: The third and most critical pillar is a new mandate for the CTO or CIO to become a strategic partner
insights.locator: Becoming a Strategic Partner in the C-Suite

insights.claim: BCG proposes a CEO diagnostic for tech leaders: measurable impact of AI inside the tech function, an estate blueprint with steps against vendor lock-in, a central dashboard and model gateways for AI tooling costs mapped to business cases, human/agent team design with HR, and embedded teams with measurement and controls.
insights.speaker: Joppe Bijlsma
insights.so_what: Checklist for diligence calls or management meetings to probe whether a company's AI program is real.
insights.locator: Key Questions for CEOs to Ask Tech Leaders

insights.claim: BCG reports that an AI-first mindset has accelerated delivery cycles of top software delivery teams by two to five times and lifted their productivity by 30% to 70%.
insights.speaker: Joppe Bijlsma
insights.so_what: Benchmark for the size of engineering-cost leverage AI-first software organizations can achieve; relevant to margin outlooks of software-heavy firms.

insights.claim: BCG says tech leaders have contributed to organization-wide AI impact such as a 5% to 10% uplift in front-office productivity.
insights.speaker: Joppe Bijlsma
insights.so_what: Front-office gains are far smaller than engineering gains, implying AI's near-term productivity edge is concentrated in tech functions.
insights.locator: Notably, we have seen tech leaders meaningfully contribute

insights.claim: At a tech hyperscaler, BCG's six-week agentic adoption sprints raised power users of agentic coding tools from 5% to 50% of an R&D team and produced an engineering productivity uplift of more than 100%, beyond what the initial tool rollout alone achieved.
insights.speaker: Joppe Bijlsma
insights.so_what: Tool licenses alone under-deliver; adoption coaching/change management drives returns, which supports demand for AI enablement services.
insights.quote: power users rose from 5% of the team to 50%
insights.locator: For example, BCG worked with a tech hyperscaler

insights.claim: BCG contends that savings from embedding AI into engineering, operations, security and data management (a 'customer zero' approach involving delayering build-and-run functions and embedding build squads in the business) can help fund the rest of a company's AI transformation.
insights.speaker: Joppe Bijlsma
insights.so_what: Expect AI programs to be self-funded via tech-function headcount/structure changes; watch for delayering in IT org announcements.

themes.theme: Agent platform and AI silent failure

insights.claim: BCG says the AI/tech function must build an enterprise AI/agent platform with telemetry, monitoring and controls, a comprehensive multi-type data layer enforcing privacy and ownership, and security-first design, typically vendor-neutral to benefit from future innovation.
insights.speaker: Joppe Bijlsma
insights.so_what: Vendor-neutral architecture preference is a headwind for single-vendor AI lock-in strategies and a tailwind for orchestration, observability and data-governance tooling.

insights.claim: According to BCG research, 75% of tech leaders fear AI 'silent failure', where AI fails to deliver value and scale beyond a single use case; BCG positions an enterprise agent platform as a key defense.
insights.speaker: Joppe Bijlsma
insights.so_what: Widespread fear of pilot purgatory signals risk to enterprise AI spend durability if platforms are not built.
insights.locator: It is an important weapon against AI “silent failure”

themes.theme: AI spend economics with the CFO

insights.claim: BCG says CTOs/CIOs should make AI-agent spending transparent, predictable and attributed so the CFO can govern it as a portfolio, including classifying it as opex, capex or cost of goods sold; for a typical company these processes can cut token costs by around 40% over 12 months.
insights.speaker: Joppe Bijlsma
insights.so_what: FinOps discipline on AI could compress token consumption per company by ~40%, a potential drag on model-provider revenue per customer and a driver for cost-management tools.
insights.quote: these processes can reduce token costs by around 40% over 12 months

insights.claim: BCG argues AI-first organizations need an agentic workforce strategy built jointly by the tech leader and CHRO, covering skills, AI-enabled career paths, agent performance assessment, governance controls as agents proliferate, and agent onboarding/offboarding processes.
insights.speaker: Joppe Bijlsma
insights.so_what: Treating agents like workforce members creates demand for agent identity, governance and HR-tech tooling.

insights.claim: A BCG/GLG study found 89% of organizations report experiencing AI-enabled attacks, making collaboration with the CRO or CISO a core part of tech leaders' remit.
insights.speaker: Joppe Bijlsma
insights.so_what: Near-universal AI-enabled attack exposure supports sustained cybersecurity budget growth tied to AI deployment.
insights.quote: 89% of organizations have reported experiencing AI-enabled attacks
insights.locator: With the Rest of the C-Suite
